extracted.intended_audience: students/readers of Plato; educators, poets, and writers interested in literary education and moral censorship
extracted.subtask_short: poetry and education in Plato's Republic
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive guidelines from Plato's Republic about what kinds of poetry, music, rhythm, imitation, and other arts are appropriate for educating guardians and shaping moral character. Emphasises censorship of immoral portrayals, musical and rhythmic simplicity, and complementary gymnastic and dietary regimes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit attributing impious actions to gods or heroes
rubrics_metrics.description: We will not have them trying to persuade our youth that the gods are the authors of evil, and that heroes are no better than men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compel the poets to declare either that these acts were not done by them, or that they were not the sons of gods; put an end to such tales lest they engender laxity of morals among the young.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forbid claims that wicked men are often happy
rubrics_metrics.description: Poets and story-tellers are guilty of making the gravest misstatements when they tell us that wicked men are often happy, and the good miserable; and that injustice is profitable when undetected, but that justice is a man’s own loss.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These things we shall forbid them to utter, and command them to sing and say the opposite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish narration from imitation (style selection)
rubrics_metrics.description: All mythology and poetry is a narration of events, either past, present, or to come; narration may be either simple narration, or imitation, or a union of the two.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide whether poets should appear as themselves (narration) or assume characters (imitation); select the mode appropriate to moral education and the subject-matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardians should imitate only virtuous characters
rubrics_metrics.description: If they imitate at all, they should imitate from youth upward only those characters which are suitable to their profession—the courageous, temperate, holy, free, and the like; but they should not depict or be skilful at imitating any kind of illiberality or baseness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid training guardians to imitate women quarrelling, those vaunting against the gods, persons in sickness, love, or labour, slaves performing slave-offices, cowards, revilers, or madmen, because imitation grows into habit and second nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: One craft per person; no pantomimic versatility for guardians
rubrics_metrics.description: One man can only do one thing well, and not many; and if he attempt many, he will altogether fail of gaining much reputation in any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guardians, dedicated wholly to maintaining freedom in the State, must not practise or imitate occupations unrelated to their craft; they should not be rhapsodists, actors, comic and tragic actors, or versatile pantomimic performers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ban imitation of certain behaviors, roles, and noises
rubrics_metrics.description: We will not allow those for whom we profess a care... to imitate a woman quarrelling with her husband, or when she is in affliction, or sorrow, or weeping... neither must they represent slaves... performing the offices of slaves... nor be trained to imitate the action or speech of men or women who are mad or bad... Nor may they imitate smiths or other artificers, or oarsmen, or boatswains... Nor may they imitate the neighing of horses, the bellowing of bulls, the murmur of rivers and roll of the ocean, thunder, and all that sort of thing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude such imitations from the education of guardians because early and repeated imitation can corrupt character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permit limited personation of good men within narration
rubrics_metrics.description: A just and good man in the course of a narration comes on some saying or action of another good man—he will be most ready to play the part of the good man when he is acting firmly and wisely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narration for virtuous speakers may include some impersonation of virtuous deeds, but overall style should be primarily narrative with only modest imitation of goodness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject pantomimic entertainers despite popularity
rubrics_metrics.description: The pantomimic... is the most popular style with children and their attendants, and with the world in general... in our State such as he are not permitted to exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although such performers may be admired elsewhere, the law will not allow their presence in the ideal State—honour them ceremonially but send them away to another city.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admit only styles that imitate virtue (prefer pure imitator of virtue)
rubrics_metrics.description: I should prefer only to admit the pure imitator of virtue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even where mixed styles are charming, the State should prioritise those styles that consistently represent virtuous models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulate musical harmonies; ban soft/relaxed harmonies
rubrics_metrics.description: The harmonies expressive of sorrow... the mixed or tenor Lydian, and the full-toned or bass Lydian... these then must be banished... drunkenness and softness and indolence are utterly unbecoming the character of our guardians... The Ionian, and the Lydian; they are termed ‘relaxed.’ Well, and are these of any military use? Quite the reverse... the Dorian and the Phrygian are the only ones which you have left.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude harmonies associated with sorrow, softness, drunkenness, or indolence (e.g., Lydian, Ionian); retain harmonies (Dorian, Phrygian) suited to courage and temperance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrict instruments to lyre and harp; ban flute and complex instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: We shall not maintain the artificers of lyres with three corners and complex scales... What do you say to flute-makers and flute-players? Would you admit them into our State... the flute is worse than all the stringed instruments put together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permit only lyre and harp in the city (shepherds may have a pipe in the country); ban panharmonic or overly complex instruments and flute-based music.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer simple, expressive rhythms; avoid complex metres
rubrics_metrics.description: We ought not to seek out complex systems of metre, or metres of every kind, but rather to discover what rhythms are the expressions of a courageous and harmonious life; and when we have found them, we shall adapt the foot and the melody to words having a like spirit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose rhythms that express courage and temperance (e.g., dactylic/heroic, iambic/trochaic when suitable); consult musical experts for classification and assignment of rhythms to character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subordinate musical elements to moral words
rubrics_metrics.description: Rhythm and harmony are regulated by the words, and not the words by them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let melody and rhythm follow the moral tone and meaning of the words; do not bend moral content to fit musical novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value simplicity of style as expression of noble character
rubrics_metrics.description: Beauty of style and harmony and grace and good rhythm depend on simplicity,—I mean the true simplicity of a rightly and nobly ordered mind and character, not that other simplicity which is only an euphemism for folly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for true simplicity in artistic expression; avoid false simplicity that denotes ignorance or folly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artists must depict beauty and virtue only; ban portrayal of vice/indecency
rubrics_metrics.description: Shall our superintendence go no further, and are the poets only to be required by us to express the image of the good in their works, on pain, if they do anything else, of expulsion from our State? Or is the same control to be extended to other artists... prohibited from exhibiting the opposite forms of vice and intemperance and meanness and indecency in sculpture and building and the other creative arts?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevent those artists who cannot conform to showing only the beautiful and virtuous from practising their art within the State, lest youth be corrupted by exposure to moral deformity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Musical training as primary means of moral formation
rubrics_metrics.description: Musical training is a more potent instrument than any other, because rhythm and harmony find their way into the inward places of the soul, on which they mightily fasten, imparting grace, and making the soul of him who is rightly educated graceful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin musical education early so that children internalise grace and develop taste to recognise and reject faults in art and nature; music shapes character before reason fully develops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gymnastic training should be simple, military, and lifelong
rubrics_metrics.description: Gymnastic as well as music should begin in early years; the training in it should be careful and should continue through life... a finer sort of training will be required for our warrior athletes, who are to be like wakeful dogs, and to see and hear with the utmost keenness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt military-style physical training and regimen suited to campaign conditions (simple food, robustness, wakefulness) rather than indulgent athletic regimens that produce fragility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dietary simplicity for guardians; avoid refined foods and indulgence
rubrics_metrics.description: Sweet sauces are nowhere mentioned in Homer... a man who is to be in good condition should take nothing of the kind... I can hardly be mistaken in saying that sweet sauces are nowhere mentioned in Homer... not approve of Syracusan dinners... Corinthian girl... Athenian confectionary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simplify diet for guardians (roast not boiled, no sweet sauces, avoid refined luxury) as complexity in diet parallels complexity and licence in music and leads to disease and moral decay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardians must abstain from intoxication
rubrics_metrics.description: That they must abstain from intoxication has been already remarked by us; for of all persons a guardian should be the last to get drunk and not know where in the world he is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make sobriety a legal and moral requirement for guardians; drunkenness is incompatible with guardianship and mutual trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excessive reliance on doctors and lawyers indicates poor education
rubrics_metrics.description: When intemperance and diseases multiply in a State, halls of justice and medicine are always being opened... Is it not disgraceful... that a man should have to go abroad for his law and physic because he has none of his own at home?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for an education and social order where citizens are self-sufficient in conduct and habit so as to avoid over-professionalisation of medicine and law caused by decadent living.
